request:
Our school library wants a simple catalogue of its books. The librarian should be able to add a book with its title, its author and how many copies the library owns. Students should be able to see all the books, and look at one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name, and returns it when they are done; a student can only return a book they actually borrowed. When every copy of a book is out, nobody else can borrow it until a copy comes back.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Can one student borrow more than one copy of the same book at a time, and is there a limit on how many books a student can have out in total?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Do borrowed books have a due date (for example 2 weeks), or can students keep them until they bring them back?
A: Not needed for now.
Q: Should only the librarian be able to add books (for example with a password), and should they also be able to edit or remove books?
A: Not needed for now.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I've built the library catalogue in `app.py`. I also wrote 6 tests covering everything you asked for, and they all pass. The books and loans are saved in a file called `library.db` in the project folder.

**What the app can do:**
- **Add a book** (`POST /books`): the librarian gives the title, author and number of copies. Title and author can't be blank, and there must be at least 1 copy.
- **See all books** (`GET /books`): every book with its copy count and how many are still on the shelf.
- **Look at one book** (`GET /books/{id}`): the same details for a single book. Asking for a book that doesn't exist returns "not found".
- **Borrow a book** (`POST /books/{id}/borrow`): the student gives their name (it can't be blank). If every copy is already out, the request is refused.
- **Return a book** (`POST /books/{id}/return`): the student gives their name. If that student doesn't currently have the book, the return is refused.

**Choices I made where you had no preference:**
- A student can borrow more than one copy of the same book, and there's no limit on how many books one student can have out.
- There are no due dates, no passwords, and no way to edit or remove books.
- Students are identified only by the name they type, so "Ann" and "Ann Smith" count as different people. To return a book, a student has to type their name exactly as they did when borrowing it.
